usage: I want to be an office worker.
examples: I am an office worker at a big company.
My older brother is an office worker at a bank.
The office worker takes the subway every morning.
nuance: 회사원 means a regular company employee who works for a private business. It is the most common answer when Koreans state their job politely.
mistakes: Saying 회사원예요 instead of correct 회사원이에요

usage: I want to be a civil servant.
I take the civil service exam.
examples: I am a civil servant working at city hall.
많은 사람이 공무원이 되고 싶어 해요.
Many people want to become civil servants.
My older sister prepares for the civil service exam.
nuance: 공무원 means a government employee who works for a public office or city hall. In Korea this job is popular because it offers strong stability.
mistakes: Confusing 공무원 with 회사원 the company worker

examples: I am a homemaker who raises children.
The homemaker goes to the market every morning.
My mother is a diligent homemaker.
nuance: 주부 means a person who manages the home and family full time. The word 전업주부 stresses that homemaking is their only full time work.
mistakes: Saying 주부이에요 instead of correct 주부예요

usage: I want to be a businessperson.
examples: I am a businessperson who started a small company.
That businessperson opened a new shop.
My uncle is a famous businessperson.
nuance: 사업가 means a person who runs or owns a business and takes financial risks. It sounds bigger than a simple shop owner, who is often called 사장님.
mistakes: Confusing 사업가 the owner with 사업 the business

usage: I want to be a designer.
examples: I am a designer who makes clothes.
That designer made a pretty bag.
My friend is a designer working at a company.
nuance: 디자이너 is the everyday borrowed word for a person who designs clothes, products, or graphics. Koreans add the field, like 옷 디자이너 or 웹 디자이너.
mistakes: Saying 디자이너이에요 instead of correct 디자이너예요

usage: I want to be a programmer.
examples: I am a programmer who makes games.
The programmer works on a computer every day.
제 동생은 프로그래머가 되고 싶어 해요.
My younger sibling wants to be a programmer.
nuance: 프로그래머 means a person who writes computer programs and code for a living. The similar word 개발자 is also very common in Korean tech workplaces.
mistakes: Saying 프로그래머이에요 instead of correct 프로그래머예요

usage: I want to be an engineer.
examples: I am an engineer who makes cars.
My older brother is an engineer at a factory.
nuance: 엔지니어 means a person who designs, builds, or fixes machines and systems. The native term 기술자 is close but can sound more like a hands on technician.
mistakes: Saying 엔지니어이에요 instead of correct 엔지니어예요

usage: I want to be a writer.
examples: I am a writer who writes novels.
That writer published a new book.
nuance: 작가 means an author who writes books, stories, or drama scripts as a profession. A news reporter is 기자 instead, so do not mix the two.
mistakes: Confusing 작가 the author with 기자 the reporter

usage: I want to be a painter.
examples: I am a painter who paints pictures.
That painter painted a beautiful picture.
My aunt is a famous painter.
nuance: 화가 means an artist who paints or draws pictures as their main work. The wider word 예술가 covers all artists, including musicians and dancers.
mistakes: Confusing 화가 the painter with 그림 the picture

usage: I want to be a professor.
examples: I am a professor teaching at a university.
The professor asked a hard question.
nuance: 교수 means a university professor who teaches and researches. When you speak to one you almost always add 님, because dropping it sounds rude.
mistakes: Confusing 교수 the professor with 선생님 the teacher

usage: I want to be an interpreter.
examples: I am an interpreter who turns English into Korean.
One interpreter came to the meeting.
The interpreter speaks two languages well.
nuance: 통역사 means a person who interprets spoken language between two languages in real time. A person who translates written text is called 번역사 instead.
mistakes: Confusing 통역사 spoken with 번역사 written

usage: I want to be a driver.
examples: I am a driver who drives a bus.
The taxi driver knows the roads well.
My father is a truck driver.
nuance: 운전사 means a person who drives a vehicle like a bus or taxi as their job. For a polite or professional tone Koreans often say 운전기사 instead.
mistakes: Confusing 운전사 the driver with 운전 the driving
